facts.fact_text: Following the February-March 2003 presidential election in Armenia, the applicant participated in a series of rallies of protest organised in Yerevan by the opposition parties.
On 7 April 2003 at 5 p.m. a demonstration was held in the centre of Yerevan on the occasion of Mother's Day.
The demonstration of 7 April 2003 took place on the Mashtots Avenue next to the Research Institute of Ancient Manuscripts (Մատենադարան).
The demonstration of 7 April 2003 appears to have been of a political nature.
The applicant took part in the demonstration of 7 April 2003.
The applicant took part in the march that followed the demonstration of 7 April 2003.
The applicant was in the front line of the march of 9 April 2003, holding the Armenian flag.
At the Central District Police Station of Yerevan, the applicant found out that she had been arrested for having participated in the demonstration of 7 April 2003.

The police officers drew up a record of an administrative offence (վարչական իրավախախտման արձանագրություն) in which it was stated that the applicant had "participated in a march and violated public order" on 7 April 2003.

Judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan, after a brief hearing, sentenced the applicant under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) to an administrative fine of 1500 Armenian drams (approximately EUR 2.4 at the material time) in relation to the events of 7 April 2003.

Judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan sentenced the applicant under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) to five days of administrative detention in relation to the events of 9 April 2003.
The applicant's actions on 7 April 2003 were qualified under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (Վարչական իրավախախտումների վերաբերյալ ՀՀ օրենսգիրք – "the CAO") as minor hooliganism.
The applicant's actions on 9 April 2003 were qualified under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) as minor hooliganism.
The applicant's actions on 7 April 2003 were qualified under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (Վարչական իրավախախտումների վերաբերյալ ՀՀ օրենսգիրք – "the CAO") as minor hooliganism.
The applicant's actions on 9 April 2003 were qualified under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) as minor hooliganism.

The applicant alleged that traffic was suspended by the traffic police on the relevant stretch of the Mashtots Avenue prior to the commencement of the demonstration of 7 April 2003 in order to facilitate its conduct.

The Government did not dispute the applicant's allegation that traffic was suspended by the traffic police on the relevant stretch of the Mashtots Avenue prior to the commencement of the demonstration of 7 April 2003.

The applicant alleged that while most of her written statement of 7 April 2003 was true, the part concerning the obstruction of traffic did not correspond to reality since the traffic had been beforehand suspended by the traffic police.

Judge M.'s entire finding in relation to the events of 7 April 2003 stated: "On 7 April 2003 between 4 p.m. and 6 p.m. ... on the Mashtots Avenue [the applicant], together with a group of people, obstructed street traffic, violated public order by making a loud noise, and incited other participants of the demonstration to do the same..."

Judge M.'s entire finding in relation to the events of 9 April 2003 stated: "On 9 April 2003 between 11 a.m. and 1 p.m. in the Central District of Yerevan [the applicant], swearing loudly and hitting passers-by, obstructed street traffic and violated public order."
The applicant alleged that her written statement of 7 April 2003 was made under pressure and was dictated to her by the police officers.
The applicant alleged that she was forced to sign the record of an administrative offence and other documents prepared by the police officers on 7 April 2003 under threat of violence.
The applicant alleged that the police officers persuaded her to refuse a lawyer on 7 April 2003 by insisting that a lawyer's involvement would not help and would only be detrimental to her case.

The applicant alleged, and the Government did not explicitly dispute, that the record of the court hearing of 7 April 2003 was a fake and was drafted at some point after the hearing in order to create an appearance of lawfulness.
The applicant alleged that in reality there was no clerk present at the court hearing of 7 April 2003 and the hearing was not being recorded.
The applicant alleged that the court hearing of 7 April 2003 lasted not more than five minutes and was conducted in Judge M.'s office.
The applicant alleged that, contrary to what the record stated, only Judge M., the applicant and the accompanying police officer were present at the court hearing of 7 April 2003.
The applicant alleged that at the court hearing of 7 April 2003, Judge M. neither explained her rights nor asked whether she wanted to have a lawyer.
The applicant alleged that at the court hearing of 7 April 2003, the materials of the case file were not read out and she was not allowed to make any oral submissions.
The applicant alleged that at the court hearing of 7 April 2003, no evidence was taken or examined.
The applicant alleged that at the court hearing of 7 April 2003, Judge M. prepared the decision solely on the basis of the materials prepared by the police.
The applicant alleged, and the Government did not explicitly dispute, that the court hearing of 9 April 2003 was in reality conducted in the same manner as the court hearing of 7 April 2003.
